Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the GlobalBank Holdings Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review GlobalBank Holdings's results for the Q2 2024. With me this morning are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Risk Officer; and Lisa Patel, Chief Credit Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. GlobalBank Holdings delivered strong performance in the Q2, driven by our commitment to customer service and operational excellence.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on:
1. Growing our core businesses
2. Investing in technology and innovation
3. Managing risk effectively
4. Optimizing our capital allocation
5. Enhancing our employee engagement.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights on our fee income growth across wealth management, investment banking, and cards; trends in operating expenses; the dynamics around our cost of deposits; the macroeconomic outlook; and the key assumptions behind our guidance. Fee income was a standout, up double digits with strength in each segment amid resilient client demand. Expenses rose modestly but stayed disciplined, supporting our efficiency targets. Our deposit costs ticked higher with competition but remain competitive thanks to our relationship focus. The macro environment shows resilience with some softening signals, and our guidance embeds prudent assumptions for continued execution.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah Thompson to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Johnathan, and good morning. GlobalBank Holdings reported net income of $1.2 billion for the Q2, or $2.45 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 8% due to loan growth and improved net interest margin. Non-interest income was up 12%. Key performance indicators include Return on Tangible Common Equity of 13.2% and an efficiency ratio of 57%. We are confident in our ability to achieve our financial goals for the year.

Let me dive deeper into some key areas starting with our fee income performance, a cornerstone of our diversified revenue stream. Total fee and commission income reached $2.85 billion, marking a 14% increase year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter. This was our strongest quarterly growth since late 2021, fueled by steady client engagement even as we navigated Fed rate stability, ongoing European inflation, and calmer equity markets following the AI surge.

Stripping out one-time items such as $150 million from prior portfolio restructurings, core fees still advanced 12%. By region, the Americas led with 18% growth, followed by 11% in EMEA and 9% in APAC, underscoring our push into fast-expanding markets like India and Southeast Asia.

In wealth management, fees hit $1.42 billion, up 16% year-over-year and making up half our fee mix, right in our 45-55% target range. Assets under management reached a record $4.8 trillion, lifted by 8% market gains, especially the S&P 500's double-digit year-to-date rise and emerging market recoveries. Organically, we added $28 billion in net new money, pacing toward our $100 billion annual target, powered by a 22% jump in high-net-worth mandates where we grabbed 15% more share from rivals through the Global Wealth Connect platform. Performance fees rose 25% to $220 million, linked to strong returns in alternatives like private credit and infrastructure at 9-11% net IRR amid energy shifts.

APAC shone with 25% fee expansion from $12 billion in net new flows from ultra-wealthy clients in China and India, backed by doubling relationship managers to 1,200 and new Sharia-compliant offerings meeting MAS standards. In the US, slight fee pressure to 65 basis points was countered by scale and our AI-driven SmartWealth Advisor, lifting cross-sell to 3.8 products per client via ESG analytics. We're ramping $500 million in tech for blockchain tokenization of assets, piloting with BlackRock's fund to draw millennials with low-entry fractional shares. We expect 12-15% growth this fiscal year with steady markets.

Investment banking fees climbed to $850 million, up 22% year-over-year and our best Q2 in years, now 30% of fees as we rose to fourth in global M&A tables per Dealogic. Advisory jumped 35% to $420 million on $180 billion in deals, including big tech consolidations like Adobe-Figma advice and European industrials amid green initiatives. ECM contributed $210 million, up 18% with 12 follow-ons despite softer IPOs, highlighted by a $5 billion semiconductor block amid AI and supply chain dynamics. DCM added $220 million, up 15%, with high-yield up 20% as spreads tightened to 95 basis points over Treasuries; in EMEA, we took 12% share in sustainable bonds totaling €8 billion under EU Taxonomy.

Our IBXpert AI tool cut pitchbook time 40% and boosted win rates to 28% using SEC and ESG data. APAC ECM faced Hang Seng swings, but our ICBC venture holds 10% in RMB bonds. With a $250 billion M&A pipeline up 30% sequentially, we guide $3.2-3.5 billion in full-year IB fees barring recession.

Cards and payments fees reached $580 million, up 8% year-over-year and 3% sequentially, 20% of the mix. Purchase volumes rose 14% to $320 billion, beating industry 9% per Nilson, via contactless and tokenization. Interchange at $350 million benefited from US fee adjustments post-Durbin, offset by premium Visa Infinite growth at 25% enrollment for $120 million in fees. Consumer cards up 10% on travel, commercial 12% from SMB cross-sell with higher tickets.

Latin America surged 20% via Brazil's Pix at 15 million transactions monthly; Europe countered PSD3 caps with services like currency conversion. CardLink AI hit 99.9% fraud accuracy, Apple/Google partnerships lifted adoption 18%. We target 4-6% growth this year, with BNPL upside via Affirm.

Overall, this 14% fee rise highlights franchise balance—wealth for stability, IB for cycles, cards for volume—with cross-sells like 20% of IB from wealth expanding fee ratio to 42%. Our $2 billion in GenAI and cloud sets us for mid-teens growth cyclically.

Next, on operating expenses, where we maintained tight control. Total expenses were $2.85 billion, up 4.2% year-over-year from $2.74 billion but flat sequentially. This improved our efficiency ratio to 56.8%, 110 basis points better year-over-year and in our 55-60% band, thanks to our transformation efforts.

Compensation and benefits at $1.42 billion, up 5.1% and 50% of opex, reflected 3.5% merit pay aligned with peers, plus incentives from high origination in IB and mortgages during rate pauses. Headcount rose 1.2% to 92,000 in growth areas like wealth and digital, offset by 4% cuts in branches via attrition. Tech hires up 8% for AI, with per-FTE comp up 3.8% versus fintechs; we see moderation to 3% next year with automation.

Occupancy and equipment at $285 million, up 2.8%, from return-to-office but mitigated by closing 45 branches and consolidating, saving $25 million toward $100 million annual goal. Utilities up 6% on inflation; $40 million in core system upgrades for FedNow.

Technology and communications jumped 12.4% to $520 million on digital shift: $150 million cloud acceleration to AWS/Azure at 65% done, 15% TCO savings; GenAI fraud tools cut false positives 30%, chatbots handle 25% inquiries. Fintech ties like Plaid/Temenos at $45 million for PSD3; APAC up 18% on UPI/Alipay.

Professional fees and regulatory at $380 million, up 3.7%, with $60 million one-offs for stress tests/Basel IV; savings from outsourcing KYC/AML to IBM/Genpact. Marketing/other at $245 million, down 1.5%, via efficient digital CAC cuts 15% on GlobalBank Go app, lower litigation.

Trailing 12-month opex grew 6.1% versus 9.2% revenue, with levers like RPA saving $80 million and 3:1 branch-to-digital shift. US up 3%, Europe 7% on DORA, APAC 10% for SME growth. Our Bank 3.0 plan with $500 million capex targets 52-55% efficiency by 2026, like Goldman/HSBC moves.

Now, shifting to our deposit franchise and cost dynamics. Average cost of deposits was 2.48% in Q2, up 23 basis points sequentially from 2.25% and 132 basis points year-over-year from 1.16%, tracking the Fed's 5.25-5.50% funds rate. Our deposit beta was 45% for interest-bearing, below money-center 55-60% due to less wholesale reliance.

Total deposits grew 4.2% to $28.7 billion, with 7% in low-cost transactional. Non-interest-bearing at 38% of mix cost 0%; interest-bearing averaged 2.98%—checking/NOW 1.85%, MMAs 3.42%, CDs 4.75%. MMA share to 22%, CDs down to 12%.

Competition heats from Ally/Marcus at 4.8-5% APY, SoFi/Chime grabbing digital share; we price MMAs at 3.90-4.35% with discounts. Peers like Fifth Third at 2.40-2.50%, Citi higher. Midwest betas under 40% via C&I ties; Southeast up 30 bps to 3.15%.

Initiatives include AI pricing for relationship tiers saving 8% beta, YieldBoost app alerts up 12% inflows, zero-beta sweeps targeting 25% commercial mix. Q3 cost to 2.65% with 15-20 bps rise; cuts could add NIM. 85% L/D, no brokered CDs.

On the macroeconomic front, our outlook points to resilience with challenges. Global GDP at 3.1% per IMF, inflation easing but core sticky. US GDP beat at 2.8% Q2, consumer strong, unemployment 4.1%, Fed cuts likely to 4.75%. NIM up 15 bps to 3.65% on 32% beta, core deposits to $850 billion.

Consumer delinquencies mild at 2.8% cards, reserves solid. CRE at 8% loans de-risked, office cautious. Europe soft at 1.2% growth, ECB cut helps but beta 40%. APAC China NPLs 1.4% offset by India 7% GDP, HDFC ties.

NII up 11% to $8.2 billion, fees steady. GenAI with Palantir saves $150 million, cloud 85% done, ESG lending $100 billion. Base: US soft land 2.5% 2025, ROE 13.5%, EPS $4.85-4.95.

Finally, our full-year 2024 guidance: adjusted EPS $8.25-8.75, 5-10% growth; PPNR 4-7%; ROTCE 12-13%. Assumptions: US GDP 2.0-2.5%, unemployment 4.3%, two Fed cuts to 4.75%, 10-year 4.10%, no recession (20% odds). NII 3-5%, NIM 3.25-3.35%, betas 35%.

Loans 4-6%: C&I 5-7%, consumer 4-5%, mortgages flat-2%, CRE 2-4%. Deposits 3-5%, L/D 78-80%. NCOs 45-55 bps, provisions $1.2 billion. Fees 5-8%, AUM $1.2 trillion. Expenses $18.2-18.6 billion, tech $850 million on AI/cloud/embedded finance. CET1 11.0-11.5% post-buybacks/dividend.

This sets us up strongly.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. As Chief Risk Officer, I would like to briefly discuss our risk management framework. We continue to prioritize proactive risk identification and mitigation. Our key focus areas include credit portfolio monitoring and cybersecurity enhancements. We remain vigilant in monitoring emerging risks and adapting our strategies accordingly.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson:
Good morning. Can you provide more detail on the drivers behind the fee income breakdown, particularly in investment banking?

Johnathan Hale:
Good morning, Mike. Absolutely, as Sarah outlined, investment banking was a highlight with 22% growth to $850 million. The M&A advisory surge on $180 billion volume, including high-profile tech and industrials deals, combined with solid ECM and DCM performance, really drove that. Our AI tools improved our competitive positioning, and the pipeline remains robust at $250 billion. We're well-positioned regardless of macro turns.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
What are your expectations for operating expenses and deposit costs heading into the back half?

Sarah Thompson:
Thanks, Emily. On expenses, we expect continued discipline with the efficiency ratio trending toward 55-60%, supported by our Bank 3.0 investments yielding savings even as tech spend ramps. Inflation is a watch but offset by automation. For deposit costs, another modest 15-20 bps rise to around 2.65% in Q3, stabilizing thereafter with our relationship pricing and digital tools keeping betas lagged. If rates ease as assumed, that supports NIM upside.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Can you comment on the credit quality of the commercial real estate portfolio?

Lisa Patel:
Good morning, David. Our CRE book, at about 8% of loans, remains high quality with focus on multifamily and industrial. We've de-risked office exposure, reduced new commitments 25%, and coverage is strong at 1.8% reserves with LTV caps. Delinquencies are low, and under our outlook, charge-offs stay sub-20 bps. Proactive management keeps us resilient.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Johnathan Hale for any closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you for your interest in GlobalBank Holdings. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
